derivation_notes: The refinement keeps the same states and processes but relaxes the assumption that the secondary transfer stage has one fixed relaxation time throughout decay. As k falls, the large-eddy reservoir weakens, so the r state is taken to relax with an effective timescale tau_transfer*(k_shutdown_scale + k)/k, which approaches tau_transfer for energetic turbulence and lengthens during depleted decay without adding new degrees of freedom.
change_summary: The secondary transfer-memory equation is made energy-level dependent by modulating its effective coefficient with k/(k_shutdown_scale + k). This produces stronger late-stage lag of r behind q, which feeds back into epsilon production and changes the target-response curvature across decay stages.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The secondary cascade stage has a turbulence-independent relaxation time tau_transfer throughout the entire decay.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Energy-level-dependent slowing of the downstream cascade occupancy adjustment during depleted turbulence, causing the secondary transfer stage to lag more strongly as k falls.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent in the energetic-support limit k/(k_shutdown_scale + k) -> 1, equivalently k >> k_shutdown_scale, where the effective secondary relaxation time returns to tau_transfer.

response_change.parent_relation: The dissipation equation uses one fixed secondary-transfer timescale tau_transfer, so for fixed initial conditions the mapping from current cascade disequilibrium states (q,r,k) to d epsilon/dt has a single characteristic lag structure throughout decay.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the fixed-lag assumption by making the downstream transfer effectiveness depend on the current turbulence level already encoded by existing states, so the mapping from (k,q,r) to d epsilon/dt changes curvature between energetic and depleted stages even without adding forcing or shear.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories that pass from k >> k_shutdown_scale to k comparable to or below that scale, epsilon(t) shows an earlier stronger memory delay and a later sharper shutdown than the parent can match with one shared fixed-lag parameter set.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable during free decay when k changes appreciably over the record, especially from k larger than k_shutdown_scale into the depleted regime where large-eddy support of downstream transfer weakens.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training the mechanism appears as mild non-exponential bending of epsilon relative to q and r at intermediate decay; in holdout it extends to later low-k stages where the same trajectories exhibit stronger transfer slowdown and sharper dissipation curvature.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the transfer-stage modulation to be constant, equivalently removing any k-dependence from the secondary transfer timescale so tau_transfer is fixed again.
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Energy-level-dependent slowing of the downstream cascade occupancy adjustment during depleted turbulence, causing the secondary transfer stage to lag more strongly as k falls.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the same fixed parameter set must now reproduce different effective r-relaxation speeds along one trajectory as k changes, creating stage-dependent curvature in epsilon through the existing nonlinear feed term rather than a uniform gain shift.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The secondary cascade stage has a turbulence-independent relaxation time tau_transfer throughout the entire decay.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The secondary cascade stage slows as turbulence is depleted, with its effective transfer coefficient reduced by the current energy-support factor k/(k_shutdown_scale + k).
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: k >> k_shutdown_scale, so k/(k_shutdown_scale + k) -> 1 and the r equation returns to (q - r)/tau_transfer.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Relative to the parent, trajectories spanning high to low k show r tracking q fairly closely early on but falling behind more strongly later, which reduces the q + C_transfer*r feed into epsilon and creates a sharper late-time bend in d epsilon/dt and thus in dk/dt = -epsilon. This is a changed target mapping, not merely an auxiliary-state change, because epsilon is an observed state entering the scored target directly.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: Refitting a single constant tau_transfer in the parent can only impose one global lag compromise for r versus q. It cannot simultaneously match the near-parent early-time transfer response when k is large and the stronger late-time slowdown when k is small, because the child introduces a state-dependent coefficient k/(k_shutdown_scale + k) that changes the relaxation law along the same trajectory rather than across separately refit parameter sets.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable during free decay when k changes appreciably over the record, especially from k larger than k_shutdown_scale into the depleted regime where large-eddy support of downstream transfer weakens.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training the mechanism appears as mild non-exponential bending of epsilon relative to q and r at intermediate decay; in holdout it extends to later low-k stages where the same trajectories exhibit stronger transfer slowdown and sharper dissipation curvature.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the transfer-stage modulation to be constant, equivalently removing any k-dependence from the secondary transfer timescale so tau_transfer is fixed again.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes the slower secondary transfer stage relaxes with one constant timescale tau_transfer regardless of turbulence level, even though spectral transfer typically slows as the large-eddy reservoir becomes too weak to maintain the same downstream filling dynamics during late decay.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The secondary cascade stage has a turbulence-independent relaxation time tau_transfer throughout the entire decay.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Energy-level-dependent slowing of the downstream cascade occupancy adjustment during depleted turbulence, causing the secondary transfer stage to lag more strongly as k falls.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the fixed-timescale assumption already present in the secondary memory equation, not to add a new process. The parent target mapping for d epsilon/dt is effectively single-phase because q and r evolve with fixed relaxation structure, so once parameters are set the shape of epsilon's delayed response over early and late decay is locked. Vary the decay stage along the observed trajectory through changing k, while holding the model form, initial conditions, and external conditions fixed. In the parent, one shared tau_transfer must compromise between matching intermediate-stage lag and late-stage shutdown. In the child, the same existing state k can modulate the transfer lag so that r tracks q more closely when turbulence is energetic but decouples more strongly as k becomes small. This changes the scored mapping because epsilon production depends explicitly on q plus C_transfer r, so altered r timing changes d epsilon/dt itself, not just an auxiliary state. The contrast is admissible when the observation window spans substantial depletion; if k remains far above k_shutdown_scale for the whole record, the refinement may be weak and the parent may be hard to distinguish.

states.rhs: -C_epsilon2*epsilon**2/k + C_cascade*(k/(k_feed_scale + k))*(k/(k_shutdown_scale + k))*k*(q + C_transfer*r)/(q_saturation + q + C_transfer*r)
states.description: Viscous dissipation rate with cascade-fed production controlled jointly by the primary memory state q and a slower secondary transfer stage r
Primary cascade-transfer memory state representing delayed adjustment of spectral energy flux toward smaller scales
Secondary slower transfer-memory state with energy-level-dependent relaxation that slows as the large-scale energy reservoir is depleted

scenario_text: Freely decaying homogeneous turbulence is represented by its turbulent kinetic energy and dissipation rate. The benchmark jointly evolves both states after external stirring is removed, with density and the large-scale domain held fixed. Energy passes from larger eddies toward smaller motions and is ultimately removed by viscosity. Mean shear, buoyancy, spatial transport, and continued forcing are excluded from the baseline dynamics.
